stepper-seven-spool.name: Seven-spool stepper rig
stepper-seven-spool.for: The rig as drawn: closed-loop NEMA 34 on a 20:1 planetary, 4 mm rope, hook-and-hook turnbuckle at the anchor. The cheapest complete machine; the turnbuckle binds first.

stepper-seven-spool-block.name: Seven-spool stepper rig with moving block
stepper-seven-spool-block.for: The same rig with the WZ 11 K block fitted, two falls: halves the drum tension and doubles what goes through the sheave, which then caps the rig.

stepper-eye-eye.name: Stepper rig, eye-and-eye anchors
stepper-eye-eye.for: The drawn rig with the anchor chain upgraded to an eye-and-eye M10 turnbuckle and 5 mm rope, so the motor sets the ceiling rather than the turnbuckle.

stepper-heavy.name: Heavy stepper rig
stepper-heavy.for: The 12 N m closed-loop NEMA 34 on the 100:1 planetary with 6 mm rope, M16 eye bolts and the M12 eye-and-eye turnbuckle: the most a stepper rig in this catalogue holds, and slow at the rope.

inverter-worm.name: Three-phase inverter rig on a worm reducer
inverter-worm.for: A 1.1 kW three-phase motor under an inverter with an encoder, 20:1 worm, 4 mm rope and the drawn anchor chain: continuous torque for a long hold, position from the encoder loop.

inverter-worm-heavy.name: Heavy inverter rig
inverter-worm-heavy.for: The 1.5 kW three-phase motor on a 30:1 worm with 6 mm rope, M16 eye bolts and the M12 eye-and-eye turnbuckle: the inverter family's strongest set here.
